name: Code Review
description: Structured code review process. Reads changes, checks correctness and conventions, and produces a structured verdict. This process is READ-ONLY — it examines code and produces feedback but NEVER modifies anything.

target.description: What to review — PR URL, branch name, or commit range (e.g. 'main..feat/new-feature')

steps.title: Read diff and understand changes
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP — do NOT modify, fix, or change any code.

Understand the changes in ${target}:
1. Get the full diff (`git diff`, `git log`, or read PR description)
2. Identify all modified files and the scope of changes
3. Read the surrounding context for each changed file — understand what the code does, not just what changed
4. Summarize the intent of the changes: what problem is being solved and how
5. Note the size and complexity of the change set

Output: summary of what changed, why, and the scope of impact.
steps.accept_criteria: All changed files identified. Intent of changes understood. Context of surrounding code read. No files were modified.

steps.title: Check correctness and logic
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP — do NOT modify, fix, or change any code.

Review ${target} for correctness:
1. Verify the logic is sound — does the code do what it claims to do?
2. Check edge cases: null/undefined handling, empty collections, boundary conditions
3. Look for potential bugs: off-by-one errors, race conditions, resource leaks, unhandled errors
4. Verify error handling is appropriate — errors should not be silently swallowed
5. Check that tests cover the new behavior and edge cases adequately
6. Look for security concerns: injection, auth bypass, data exposure

Output: list of correctness findings, each with severity (critical/warning/nit) and specific line references.
steps.accept_criteria: Logic reviewed for soundness. Edge cases and error handling checked. Security concerns evaluated. Findings documented with severity and line references. No files were modified.

steps.title: Check conventions and patterns
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP — do NOT modify, fix, or change any code.

Review ${target} for consistency with project conventions:
1. Naming conventions — variables, functions, files follow existing patterns
2. Code organization — new code placed in appropriate modules/directories
3. Style consistency — matches the surrounding code style (not just linter rules)
4. Documentation — public APIs, complex logic, and non-obvious decisions are documented
5. Dependencies — no unnecessary new dependencies introduced
6. Performance — no obvious performance regressions (unnecessary loops, missing indexes, unbounded queries)

Output: list of convention findings, each with severity (warning/nit) and specific suggestions.
steps.accept_criteria: Naming, organization, style, and documentation checked against project conventions. Findings documented with severity. No files were modified.

steps.title: Produce review verdict
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP — do NOT modify, fix, or change any code.

Produce a structured review verdict for ${target}:

1. **Verdict**: One of: `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, or `REJECT`
   - APPROVE: No critical issues, code is ready to merge (nits are acceptable)
   - REQUEST_CHANGES: Issues found that should be fixed before merge
   - REJECT: Fundamental design or approach problems requiring rework

2. **Summary**: 2-3 sentence overview of the changes and review outcome

3. **Critical Issues**: Must-fix items blocking approval (if any)

4. **Suggestions**: Non-blocking improvements (if any)

5. **Nits**: Minor style/preference items (if any)

Format the verdict clearly so it can be posted as a review comment.
steps.accept_criteria: Structured verdict produced with clear APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/REJECT decision. All findings from previous steps incorporated. Verdict is actionable and specific. No files were modified.
